Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Evaluated Hosted API first (quick integration, prototyping), now in procurement for Dedicated reserved capacity. Primary goal: replace third-party embeddings + homegrown reranker with unified Redwood stack to reduce tail latency and token costs.

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2025-11-20: Intro discovery call (Jordan, Priya). Customer pain: spikes in per-session latency, unpredictable token spend from hosted embeddings provider.
- 2025-12-01: Hosted API trial started (search/embedding pipeline) — initial integration via SDK.
- 2026-01-12: Internal benchmark results from hosted trial: embeddings cost ~1.4x target, p95 chat latency ~320ms (off-hosted infra variability).
- 2026-02-15: Dedicated demo + architecture workshop (Priya, SE team). Fireflies id ff_2026-02-15_3921.
- 2026-02-28: Proposed Dedicated pilot (4 vGPU-equivalent pool) sent to BriarShore (drive:/BriarShore/Redwood/Dedicated_Pricing_Proposal_v3.pdf).
- 2026-03-03: Security questionnaire submitted; started SOC2 + SSO/SAML verification (drive:/BriarShore/Redwood/Security_FAQ_2026-03-03.docx).
- 2026-03-07: Pricing/concession call with CFO and Head of Ops; discussed commit levels and burst.
- 2026-03-09: Legal raised SLA and data residency items (legal hold).

Use-case & requirements (customer language / notes):
- Workloads: interactive in-app chat (primary), embeddings for semantic search, reranking stage for top-k results, scheduled summarization for weekly digest.
- Performance targets: p95 latency <= 180ms for chat token generation at 8k avg session length; sustained throughput target 120-150 QPS across peak shards.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; target blended unit cost target ~<$50 per 1M tokens (benchmarking request).
- Model preferences: open-weight family (Llama2-like / community open models), Redwood-verified quantized variants acceptable. Want ability to route to cheaper quantized fallback for low-criticality flows.
- Routing/fallback: prefer smart routing by latency/cost tier; automated fallback to smaller-quantized model when Dedicated pool saturated.
- Data/security: require SSO/SAML, audit logging retained 12 months, customer-managed KMS, VPC peering for private traffic, data residency for EU customers (some accounts).

POC / Pilot scope:
- Hosted API: validated integration, evaled quality parity.
- Dedicated pilot: 4 vGPU-equivalent pool for 4 weeks, production shadowing on 20% traffic. Success metrics: p95 latency < 200ms, cost per session <= target, no data egress incidents.

Pricing & packaging negotiation notes (core of procurement):
- Customer preference: Dedicated reserved capacity with predictable monthly commitment (vGPU-equivalent hours or committed token baseline).
- Proposed Redwood offering (internal): 4 vGPU-equivalent reserved pool, monthly commit, 12-month term with early ramp schedule. Base price quoted in proposal v3.
- Customer counter-asks:
  * 6-12 month ramp schedule: start at 40% commit for first 2 months, 70% months 3-4, 100% month 5 onward.
  * Burst allowance: up to 2x committed capacity for limited windows (72 hours per month) without immediate overage penalties; any additional burst billed at 1.3x base rate.
  * Overage pricing: prefer soft overage with monthly true-up and rollover credits for under-utilization (e.g., unused committed GPU-hours can roll to next month up to 2 months).
  * Price protection: lock-in per-token equivalent price for 12 months with CPI-style escalator capped at 3%/yr.
  * Discount asks: 15-20% discount on base Dedicated rate in exchange for 12-month commitment and case study permission.
  * Ramp credits: request initial onboarding discount / free burst credits for first 30 days of pilot.
- Redwood negotiation positions discussed internally (Priya/Jordan):
  * Flexible ramp OK, allow 3-month step-up schedule rather than immediate 40%/70% steps.
  * Burst: allow limited monthly buffer (48 hours) free, extended burst at 1.25x.
  * Overage: bill at 1.5x base for ad-hoc overages but offer monthly reconciliation & carry-forward credits for unused portions.
  * Discounts: can offer 12% on the quoted base for 12-month commitment; additional trade (case study + reference) could move to 18%.
  * SLA: standard enterprise SLA + option to attach stricter SLOs for additional fee; legal to confirm liability caps.

Open questions / blockers called out by customer: 
- Need mapping from committed capacity -> equivalent per-token pricing (engineering ask).
- Clarity on egress costs (who pays in multi-cloud setup).
- Legal: require 99.95% uptime guarantee for critical routes, and indemnity language around model outputs.
- Security: confirm audit log retention and KMS key lifecycle procedures.

Customer quotes / vibe: 
- CTO (Elena Morales): "We need predictable unit economics — surprise overages break our margins. If you can give a firm ramp + burst construct, we'll commit."
- Head of Ops: "If Dedicated brings p95 down to <200ms and costs drop 20%, this becomes a no-brainer. But finance needs clear month-by-month burn modeling."

Action items (short):
- Send revised term sheet w/ alternative ramp 3-step option, burst 48h free, overage at 1.25x and carry-forward credit language (Jordan). Target send by 2026-03-12.
- SE (Priya) to provide mapping doc: committed vGPU-hours -> token equivalence & sample cost model per flow. Due 2026-03-14.
- Finance/solutions to draft month-by-month burn model for CFO (spreadsheet attached in drive).
- Legal to provision redline of SLA and indemnity by 2026-03-18.
